content.title: Luke Kennard steps up for Lakers, leads way to Game 1 win vs. Rockets
content.text: April 18, 2026Updated April 19, 2026, 12:18 a.m. ETThe 2026 NBA postseason is finally here after a thrilling Play-In Tournament saw the Phoenix Suns, Orlando Magic, Philadelphia 76ers and Portland Trail Blazers officially earn their spot in the playoffsThe postseason action continues on Saturday as the Houston Rockets visited the Los Angeles Lakers in Game 1 of the first round. We've got you covered on everything you need to know.Want to see the full National Basketball Association schedule for April 18 and how to watch all the games? Check out our sortable NBA schedule to filter by team or division. Final: Lakers 107, Rockets 98LeBron James led the Los Angeles Lakers past the Houston Rockets, 107-98, in Game 1 of their first-round Western Conference playoff series at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.The 41-year-old James had 19 points, 13 assists, eight rebounds — and a lot of help.Reserve guard Luke Kennard was vital, too, scoring a game-high 27 points and shooting 5-for-5 from 3-point range. Kennard's performance was even more important with Lakers leading scorers Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves on the bench with injuries while Rockets starter Kevin Durant also missed the game with an injury. What LeBron James said after Lakers' victoryDuring a postgame interview with Mike Trudell of Spectrum SportsNet, LeBron James said Luke Kennard was “poised.’’“Poised, ready for the moment and we need everybody to step up, and he stepped up big time,’’ James said.It wasn’t that Kennard was 5-for-5 from 3-point range while scoring a game-high 27 points. James said every shot was “timely.’’“Especially in the fourth quarter,’’ he added.Of the Lakers’ success in Game 1, James said, “You’ve got to be able to keep your composure. Playoffs is about runs, a lot of ups and downs, a lot of obstacles. You’ve got to be able to keep your composure and stay even keeled. … It was a good first test for us.’’ Rockets vs. Lakers highlights Rockets vs. Lakers statsHere are the game leaders from each team: Houston RocketsPoints: Alperen Sengun, 19Rebounds: Jabari Smith Jr., 12Assists: Reed Sheppard, 8Steals: Amen Thompson, Tari Eason, 3Blocks: Alperen Sengun, Amen Thompson, Reed Sheppard, 1 Los Angeles LakersPoints: Luke Kennard, 27Rebounds: Deandre Ayton, 11Assists: LeBron James, 13Steals: Rui Hachimura, 3Blocks: Rui Hachimura, Marcus Smart, 2 Numbers updateKennard is 5-for-5 from 3-point range and leads all scorers with 27 points. Each of the other Lakers starters are in double-figures too. Lakers rollingJames sent the crowd into a frenzy with his first 3-pointer of trhe night. It put the Lakers up 85-72, and the decibel level spiked again on the Lakers' next possession. That's when Kennard drained a 3-pointer and put Los Angeles up 88-72 -- a16-point lead taht was its biggest of the night. End of 3Q: Lakers 75, Rockets 66The Lakers did not leave their hearts in the locker room before the second half. It was a chance for the Rockets to pounce, but the Lakers played with intensity and verve. Kennard found his rhythm again and leads the Lakers in scoring wiht 18 points. The Lakers now are shooting a mortal 57 percent from the field and Houston is shooting a ghastly 33 percent from the field. Game scoring leadersRockets: Amen Thompson, 15 pointsLakers: Luke Kennard, 18 points Get the whistles outHouston's Jae'Sean Tate did his best Draymond Green impersonation, arguging after he got whistled for a technical foul. Trust me, he deserved it: Tate got tied up with Lakers guard Marcus Smart and yanked him to the floor.Lakers forward Jake LaRavia might have gotten away with a flagrant foul after chasing down Houston's Amen Thhompson, blocking the shot and helping knock Thompson to the floor. Key moment?Houston's Reed Sheppard opened the second half with a 3-pointer, putting the Rockets up 51-50 -- their first lead in what felt like decades. Suddenly James looked 41. Well, he is 41. And athe looks looked a little listless, or frazzled, or something unfortunate. But the Lakers fought back, outscoring the Rockets 10-5 and leading 60-56 during a media timeout about halfway through the third quarter.Were the Lakers in positon to be subdued? It's hard to know with the Rockets shooting 33 percent (18-for-54) from the field. Halftime: Lakers 50, Rockets 48The Lakers came out scorching hot on offense, shooting 79 percent from the field in the first quarter. An alley oop dunk from Deandre Ayton put the Lakers up 48-38 with less than five minutes in the second quarter. But the Lakers have cooled off and the Rockets are heating up.LeBron James has had a memorable half. He's got 10 assists, six points on 3-for-7 shooting, one steal and a block. Houston RocketsPoints: Alperen Sengun, 11Rebounds: Jabari Smith Jr., Alperen Sengun, Tari Eason, 4Assists: Amen Thompson, 5Steals: Josh Okogie, Tari Eason, 2Blocks: Amen Thompson, 1 Los Angeles LakersPoints: Deandre Ayton, 12Rebounds: Deandre Ayton, 4Assists: LeBron James, 10Steals: LeBron James, Rui Hachimura, Marcus Smart, Jake LaRavia, 1Blocks: Marcus Smart, 2 How long can they keep this up?The Lakers are shooting 73 percent from the floor (19-of-26) halfway through the second quarter and lead 44-36. They're defense is less astounding. Although Los Angeles full of hustle, the Rockets look capable of beaking out offensively even though they're shooting only 46 percent from the floor. End of 1Q: Lakers 33, Rockets 29It's hard to imagine a better start for the Lakers with their two top scorers, Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, out with injuries. The Lakers have made 15 of 19 shots from the floor -- that a clip of 79 percent -- and Luke Kennard leads all scorers with 11 points on 5-for-6 shooting. LeBron James already has eight assists. EIGHT! But the Rockets have no reason to be discouraged, especially considering Kevin Durant is out with a knee injury. Despite the Lakers' lights-out shooting, Houston was 11-of-21 shooting from the floor and remains within striking distance. Lakers vs Rockets match stats: Game Leading ScorersHouston: Jabari Smith Jr.: 8 pointsLos Angeles: Luke Kennard: 11 points Haven't forgetten the RocketsFor all the Lakers lights-out shooting, the Rockets are within striking distance of their first-round opponent. So which team is finally going to lock down defensively? LeBron James stats: Let's update those numbersJames now has eight assists. With 2:52 left in the first quarter. Which means he's on pace for about 40 assists. Uh, mathematically speaking. Eye on LeBron JamesThe crowd James once wore probably belongs in a museum. He doesn't always look like basketball royalty at age 41. But in addition to making both of his shot sfrom the floor, James had a game-high four assists with the leaders leading 17-14 halfway through the first quarter. Lakers sizzlingThe Lakers have made seven of their first eight shots from the field, including two baskets by LeBron James. But the Rockets are warming up after a rough start and have pulled withhin 17-12. Kevin Durant out with knee injuryHouston Rockets star Kevin Durant, the team's leading scorer with 26 points per game, has been ruled out of Game 1 with a knee injury suffered during practice this week. The severity of the injury, right knee contusion, did not become clear publicly until game time neared. ABC's Lisa Salters reported the Rockets are hopeful that because Game 2 is Tuesday, the extra three days of rest will allow Durant to play then. Some more background on the situation.Talk about a loss of starpower, with the Lakers best player, Luka Doncic, and his backcourt mate, Austin Reaves, also are out with injuries.
